headline: Paper gives a graph-based guarantee for integrating parallel agent edits
summary: The paper formulates parallel agent edits as verified proposal integration: each proposed change is tested alone against a common starting artifact, and a dependency graph certifies which edits can be combined without interacting objective terms. It proves that fractional-coloring integration retains at least a 1/χ_f(G) fraction of total verified singleton improvement, with a matching worst-case bound for mergers restricted to selecting from the same proposals; geometric convergence follows under additional local-improvement and block-error assumptions. In structured experiments, fractional integration retained 922 units of graph-cut improvement versus 799 for a coloring fixed before proposals across 90 road-network comparisons, but adaptive ordinary coloring matched 922. A separate induced-conflict route-search schedule reduced measured wall time by a median 15% across 12 paired runs; route cost improved in four, tied in five and worsened in three. Results are author-reported and depend on explicit objective and dependency assumptions.
